why: All three checks pass; the divergence survives, with two wording corrections. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/output-styles.md line 55 is exactly "Project output styles load from every `.claude/output-styles/` between the working directory and the repository root. {/* min-version: 2.1.178 */}As of v2.1.178, when more than one of these nested directories defines a style with the same name, Claude Code uses the one closest to the working directory." The whole line was read; the second sentence sharpens the first rather than reversing it, and the surrounding <Step> (:49-53) lists the three levels user / project / managed-policy. (2) CITED CODE: packages/shared/src/prompts/output-styles.ts:210-232 outputStyleDirectories pushes exactly three paths -- USER_OUTPUT_STYLES_DIR, then join(workspaceRootPath, '.nessy-agent/output-styles'), then join(workingDirectory, '.nessy-agent/output-styles') gated on projectTrusted === true. There is no loop, no dirname climb, no repository-root discovery: the two project endpoints are sampled and nothing between them is read. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER: the only consumers are discoverCustomOutputStyles (:465-508, the sole reader of outputStyleDirectories), reached from listOutputStyles (:518) and resolveOutputStyle (:526) -> resolveOutputStyleComposition (:564), called on every prompt build at prompts/system.ts:439. Nothing upstream covers the gap: capabilities/native-sources.ts:1013-1060 enumerates the project tier ('.nessy-agent/skills', 'agents', 'mcp.json', 'hooks.json', 'permissions.json', 'MEMORY.md', 'rules') and has NO output-styles entry, and capabilities/runtime-output-styles.ts handles PLUGIN styles only (readPluginOutputStyleSources over a pinned bundle), never project directories. So a style in an intermediate package directory really is invisible. The repo even owns the missing primitive -- projectAncestors(cwd, repoRoot) at workflows/workflow-loader.ts:159, used at :244 to load workflows from every ancestor '.nessy-agent/workflows' -- so this is an unwalked path in one subsystem, not an architectural impossibility. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- none touches output styles. NOT a rename/gateway/subscription product difference either: the directory rename to '.nessy-agent/output-styles' is a separate registered row (deviation register :238) and the absence of an ancestor walk is independent of it. The finding's own provenance checks out: deviation register line 230 is this row, harvested from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-output-style-contract.md:200 section 6 'The rows we do not implement' -- i.e. a confirmed, dated, recorded divergence, which is what the register is for. TWO CORRECTIONS to the claimed our-state. (a) 'Precedence is also inverted relative to the page' is wrong and the same sentence concedes it: discoverCustomOutputStyles:497-500 comments 'Later directories outrank earlier ones' and styles.set overwrites, with the working directory pushed last, so the closest-to-cwd winner MATCHES the page for the pair we do read. Only the array's ordering convention (lowest precedence first) is inverted, which is not a behavioural divergence. (b) The claim omits the trust gate: the working-directory endpoint is read ONLY when projectTrusted === true (:227), so on an untrusted project we read one project directory, not two, and the cwd's own style is skipped. That gate is deliberate and documented at :200-209 -- an app-global selection used to resolve working-directory-first and ungated, so opening a repository that shipped a same-id style substituted its prose into the system prompt. Any fix that adds the ancestor walk must keep every walked directory behind the same gate.
